articles.title: Russian billionaire’s $600 million high-tech superyacht, dubbed ugliest in the world, is ‘stuck’ in Italy; it takes $11 million a year to keep its systems running
articles.description: Italy seized Sailing Yacht A, the $600 million superyacht owned by Russian billionaire Andrey Melnichenko, in Trieste in March 2022 under sanctions, and has been paying for its upkeep ever since. The upkeep reportedly costs about $30,000 a day, which covers a 20-person crew, fuel and climate control. The power can’t be switched off because the yacht holds paintings by Claude Monet and other artists that would deteriorate without stable temperature and humidity.

articles.description: Struggling cannabis farmers in Arizona are looking to convert old cannabis farms into mini data centres. articles.title: 'We haven't ruled it out...': Markwayne Mullin leaves cyberattack theory open in US aviation outage
articles.description: US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin on Friday (local time) said authorities had found no evidence so far that a telecommunications outage which triggered a nationwide Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop was caused by a cyberattack or rogue artificial intelligence, but stressed that investigators were not ruling out any possibility. Responding to whether he could say with 100 per cent certainty that the disruption was not caused by a cyberattack or rogue AI, Mullin said the available evidence pointed towards a mechanical failure, although investigations were continuing. 'There's nothing completely certain right now. It doesn't appear that way. We've activated our teams...This is a national emergency. We have all of our assets...There is nothing that indicates it yet,' Mullin said.

articles.title: Tired of paying for cloud storage every month? pCloud’s Black Friday Lifetime deal is the cure for subscription fatigue
articles.description: Software used to be a one-time purchase, but over time, with the addition of cloud storage and services, everything has become a subscription. One company even tried to make your car seat heaters a subscription. Count the subscriptions you’re paying for right now: iCloud, a password manager, a couple of streaming services, a music service, maybe a VPN, and whatever other app decided this year that it needed to be $4.99 per month for something that used to be a one-time purchase. Everything is a service now, and a lot of people are hitting the point where one more monthly charge is one too many on principle alone. Cloud storage is the one that’s hardest to cancel, because your photos and files are in it. That’s exactly why pCloud’s Lifetime plans are worth a look this Black Friday: you pay once, and your storage is yours for life! more…

articles.title: NASA deliberately crashed a spacecraft into an asteroid in 2022; Europe's Hera probe has now reached the impact site to measure how successfully humanity can deflect a space rock
articles.description: ESA's Hera spacecraft has initiated its observations of the Didymos asteroid system following NASA's DART mission's collision with Dimorphos. This investigation seeks to analyze the impact's effects on Dimorphos' structure and its trajectory, which is essential for planetary defense. Researchers aim to uncover the momentum enhancement factor and physical effects of the collision, while also deploying CubeSats for comprehensive data collection on both asteroids.
